title: Touch screen accessibility: screen readers and text size
when: The phone app must work with the built in phone screen readers, large system text and zoom, not only with sighted single finger use.
prompt:
Goal: The core flows work with a phone screen reader using swipe and double tap, at 200 percent text size and with pinch zoom.
Steps:
1. Swipe order follows DOM order: put markup in reading order and avoid CSS order or absolute positioning that reorders meaning.
2. Native elements first: <button>, <a href>, <input> with <label>; icon only buttons get aria-label.
3. Size text in rem and let containers grow: no fixed heights on cards, buttons or bars; test with the system font size at its largest.
4. Keep pinch zoom: never set maximum-scale=1 or user-scalable=no.
5. After a route change move focus to the new screen h1 (tabindex="-1") and update document.title.
6. Announce async results in an aria-live="polite" region: "3 items saved".
7. Every swipe or drag action has a button alternative reachable by the screen reader.
8. Group card content so one swipe reads the whole card, with the main link wrapping the title.
Quality bar:
- Each control reads as name, role and state.
- Nothing is clipped at large text sizes.
Pitfalls:
- Custom div buttons that the reader skips.
- Toasts that vanish before they are read.
- Labels that say "button" twice.
Verify:
- [ ] Every control has an accessible name.
- [ ] The viewport allows zoom.
- [ ] An aria-live region exists for status.
- [ ] Large text test noted in the findings.
Output: fixed HTML and CSS plus a findings list per screen.

examples.input: testar meu app com leitor de tela no celular
examples.output: Findings per screen, focus to h1 on route change, aria-live status, rem text, zoom allowed
